channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Google loses landmark constitutional challenge in Canadian adtech probe
item.description: Google has failed to convince Canada’s Competition Tribunal that the country’s antitrust watchdog breached its constitutional rights by exposing it to a potential record penalty.

item.title: Everybody’s a critic: The Tipline for 5 March 2026
item.description: Federal and state enforcers may not be the only US obstacles for Paramount/Warner Bros Discovery. A Los Angeles County supervisor has called for a comprehensive economic impact study of the $111 billion merger. “The entertainment industry is once again facing a merger that could hurt competition, limit the diversity of storytellers, and send ripple effects across our signature industry,” said Lind...

item.title: Live Nation tours a necessity, DC concert operator says
item.description: An independent concert operator has testified that he was “concerned” about booking enough concerts to survive without Live Nation.

item.title: Dems propose extraordinary meatpacking divestitures
item.description: Senate Democrats have introduced legislation that would require the Federal Trade Commission to break up the largest meatpacking conglomerates by establishing bright-line rules against vertical integration and concentration.

item.title: Insurance risk: The Briefing for 6 March 2026
item.description: The Spanish antitrust agency has searched several insurance companies as it investigates a potential conspiracy. No businesses have yet confirmed the raids, but the enforcer has previously looked into the market, issuing price-fixing fines in 2010 to several insurers. Also in The Briefing, Brazil progresses a gun-jumping complaint into Azul and American Airlines, and Korean investigators recommend...

item.title: Yon-Courtin: Independent EU antitrust agency proposal is “ambitious” but “feasible”
item.description: Creating an EU competition watchdog separate from the European Commission will not be easy and would require changes to the EU Treaties, but is a “necessity” given growing political interference in antitrust issues, says the lawmaker spearheading the proposal.

item.title: UK parliamentary committee explores potential outbound screening regime
item.description: An influential parliamentary committee is seeking views on the “merits and risks” of establishing an outbound investment screening regime targeting UK projects overseas, including in China.

item.title: Apple set to learn its fate in ACM dating app case
item.description: The Dutch competition authority will decide before the end of this month whether Apple must comply with a postponed order challenging commission rates imposed on dating app providers – with potential multi-million-euro fines on the cards if it fails to fall in line.

item.title: Seatgeek CEO: Exclusive deals industry “standard”
item.description: Live Nation has argued that its primary ticketing rival, SeatGeek, also mandates exclusivity from venues that host concerts and sporting events.

item.title: Friday night lights: The Tipline for 6 March 2026
item.description: Antitrust issues are not just plaguing collegiate sports. Software company Hudl has been accused of locking nearly 20,000 US high schools into its sports video analytics monopoly by acquiring 18 adjacent companies since 2011. Also in Tipline, President Donald Trump railed against NCAA v Alston during his “Saving College Sports” roundtable.
